description:
There is no inliner anywhere in the tree (verified: no inline pass in compiler2, ir_codegen, ir_dce or fz_ir; Cranelift has no cross-function inliner; the two port_planner_test.rs 'inlined' TODOs are unimplemented). So every runtime-library wrapper over an intrinsic is a real call.

This is already the case at HEAD, independent of any operator work:

  fn left >= right, do: fz_op_gte(left, right)

compiles to its own executable -- 'fn fz_op_gte__e9' appears as a standalone
Cranelift function in the single-clause build, reached by a call. Same for every
comparison and arithmetic operator, and for the thin Enum/List wrappers.

These are the easiest possible inline case: a body that is exactly one call to a
primitive the backend already special-cases by name (prim.rs carries 31 such
arms). Inlining them would remove a call per operator use across every program,
and it is the mechanism that pays back the dispatch cost fz-5xp.18 accepts by
giving the comparison operators typed clause families.

Doing it generically also replaces bespoke lowering: the reason codegen
hand-wrote a both_int/promote coercion for ordering was to avoid exactly this
call. A general 'inline a single-expression body whose tail is an intrinsic'
rule serves the whole runtime library rather than six operators.

Not a blocker for anything in fz-5xp -- correctness does not depend on it. Filed
so the cost fz-5xp.18 accepts is tracked rather than assumed away.
title: Inline single-expression runtime-library wrappers over intrinsics
